sentence: This project tests how accurately an imaging method can diagnose hepatocellular carcinoma and show how the tumor responds to treatment in animal models.
This project tests whether CRISPR technology can target only bladder cancer cells by bringing a split endonuclease together at structural variant junctions.
This project studies how melanoma cells make keratinocytes release factors that help melanoma cells migrate, invade and resist drugs.
This project provides laboratory expertise and specialized assays to researchers who study HIV.
This project studies how neurotransmitters change the electrical activity of myocytes in the infarcted heart.
This project builds imaging techniques and sensor hardware using magnetic resonance imaging to improve the diagnosis of cancer and other diseases.
This project studies how stress and lifestyle affect brain and cognitive health in middle-aged adults who are at higher risk of cognitive decline.
This project brings together chemistry and engineering to find and design small molecules that target signaling pathways in cancer.
This project tries to find out how a family of innate immune sensor proteins detects viruses and starts antiviral responses.
This project studies how arteriviruses use the neonatal Fc receptor to enter cells, damage the immune system and reach the fetus across the placental barrier.
This project studies how a human risk gene controls smooth muscle cells that drive plaque growth in atherosclerosis.
This project studies how polyethoxylated surfactants found indoors cause metabolic problems such as obesity in zebrafish.
This project studies how alternative splicing of genes is controlled and how it goes wrong in human disease.
This project tries to find genetic causes of infantile epilepsies and studies how these findings affect infants with epilepsy and their families.
This project studies how opioid use changes the brain to promote relapse using an opioid self-administration mouse model.
This project studies how disulfide modified antigens trigger autoimmune T cell responses and how redox regulation affects their presentation.
This project studies how chronic inhalation of cobalt or cobalt-oxide nanoparticles affects the lung using a three-dimensional lung model.
This project builds deep learning tools that predict survival and kidney recovery in patients with acute kidney injury on continuous renal replacement therapy.
This project provides genome editing services, such as making edited cell lines and CRISPR-modified rodent models, to cancer researchers.
This project studies how neurons in the hippocampus replay experiences during sleep and how sharp-wave ripples help stabilize memories.
